note: v15: v13 + a build that matches what the deck produces. v13 committed to Flush in 25 of 29 losses (any joker mentioning a suit, or one Jupiter, was enough) while final plays were Pair/Two Pair/High Card, and the flush suit flip-flopped between shops. Now build.decide samples 24 deals of hand size + 3 cards (jokers and levels included) and commits to the hand family with the largest share of best-play score (Flush also at 25%+ with a flush joker): matches the best play in real ante 3+ hands 56% vs 42%. A levelled hand counts as a main hand only once played twice. A paid Celestial pack takes the planet with the biggest measured gain instead of skipping. v14's wall/flat-discount shop is dropped (trailed v13).
rules: Balatro: reach each blind's chip target before hands run out. A hand scores chips x mult; jokers add chips or mult, or multiply mult (xMult). Discards are free but limited. Interest: $1 per $5 held at round end, max $5 (at $25).

instructions.blind: Should we play or skip the upcoming blind?
instructions.play_now: Should we play our strongest hand (`strongest_play`) now instead of discarding first to build a better one? `best_draw_by_measurement` compares the best draw plan with playing now: its average includes misses, and poor_draw_next_play shows downside. Weigh the measured improvement and chance of meeting pace against spending one of our remaining discards. Preserve discards when we are on pace and the improvement is small. Survival this round comes before build preference.
instructions.best_play: Which play is best this turn? `estimated_score` already includes our jokers (except any in `jokers_not_in_estimates`), but are approximate. Prefer the higher score unless a lower one keeps stronger cards or avoids resetting a scaling joker.
instructions.best_discard: If we discard, which plan best helps us survive this round? Options are ordered by measured survival value. Each models our best next play after the draw, including misses and cards held for joker effects. Prefer better average score and downside; with one hand left, prefer the chance to clear. These are sampled scoring estimates, so account for unmodeled joker effects. Use build fit only to break close choices, never to justify a clearly worse survival outlook.
instructions.item_value: How much would taking the item in `item` (described in this question) strengthen this run? `measured_gain` is its measured effect on the scores of our recent hands, jokers included: trust it for the immediate effect and add what it cannot see (scaling over the run, money, risk, future hands). `use` says what a tarot or spectral would do for us; `worth` says what a voucher gives for the rest of the run. Favour items that fit `our_build`. Consider `engine.missing`, `upcoming_boss` and what it costs. `readiness` compares our typical hand with what the next blinds need per hand and `plan` says whether to spend on power or save; `readiness_after` is the measured lift.

options.blind_play: Play the {name} (need {score} chips) and earn its cash reward
options.blind_skip: Skip the {name} to gain the {tag_name}: {tag_effect}. Skipping forgoes the blind's money and shop visit.
